questions.question: Why is "You are an expert customer support agent" considered a weak role?
options: Models ignore roles entirely, so any role is wasted text
It gives no information about the company, audience, channel, goal, or limits of authority
Roles must always be written in the user message, not the system prompt
The word "expert" causes models to refuse simple questions
questions.explanation: A useful role describes the situation: organisation, audience, emotional context, goal, and what the assistant may not do. A bare job title leaves all of that to guesswork.

questions.question: Which item most clearly belongs in the user message rather than the system prompt?
options: The rule that the assistant cannot promise claim amounts
The default tone and target audience
The specific customer email being answered in this turn
The escalation process for questions the policy does not cover
questions.explanation: Persistent context (identity, tone, limits, escalation) goes in the system prompt; the specific document or request for this turn goes in the user message.

questions.question: A prompt says "NEVER USE ALL CAPS IN REPLIES!!!". What is the recommended rewrite for modern models?
options: Repeat the rule three times so it is not missed
Delete it, because models never use capitals
Add "or you will be penalised" to increase compliance
"Avoid all-caps and exclamation marks, because customers read them as shouting."
questions.explanation: Modern models follow instructions literally and generalise from reasons, so a calm instruction with an explanation works better than shouting.

questions.question: Which practice helps keep a production system prompt maintainable?
options: Organise it into sections such as role, audience, rules, and output format, and keep it in version control
Store API keys in it so the model can call other services
Add a new special-case rule every time a single output looks wrong
Keep contradictory rules so the model can choose the best one
questions.explanation: Clear sections, version control, and re-testing on change keep prompts maintainable. Secrets should never be placed in prompts, and piles of special cases or contradictions degrade behaviour.
